claims.text: The artifacts describe the same trip and satisfy the rider's initial showing under POL-RD-08(a): EV-TRIP-00102, EV-GPS-00102 and EV-FARE-00102 all carry trip_id TRP-00102; the trip record's started_at (2026-07-19T11:23:30+08:00) is identical to the trace's first_fix_at, and the ledger's charged_at (11:55:48) sits immediately after the trace's last_fix_at (11:55:30). Same vehicle, same rider, same trip.

Under POL-RD-01 the governing distance figure is the trace, not the rounded convenience copy: gps_trace.trace_distance_km is 21.79 km against trip_record.actual_distance_km of 21.8 km, and the platform's own derived block measures the excess over the 20.4 km optimal at 1.39 km, or 6.81%. On the governing figure the excess clears the absolute limb (1.39 km > 0.8 km) but not the relative limb (6.81% < 20%), and POL-RD-01 requires both to pass. The rider is candid that a distance deviation is therefore not established and does not press a POL-RD-02 recomputation. What the rider does contest is the driver's justification for leaving the booked corridor at all.

The driver's account rests on a BKE crawl, and there is nothing behind it. The only advisory artifact, EV-ADVIS-00102-01, is MISSING — weight_multiplier 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT (BLOCKING) — and its own issue detail states that no LTA advisory covers the BKE or the Upper Bukit Timah corridor in the 11:16-11:55 window on 19 July 2026. That absence is itself citable. Without an advisory the driver cannot satisfy the three limbs of POL-RD-03: there is no advisory naming an affected road or segment, no validity window, and no shortest_lawful_alternative_km from which the capped justified excess could be computed. POL-RD-08 then provides that a general assertion that traffic was bad, unsupported by a traffic_advisory ID, does not discharge the driver's burden.

The diversion was the driver's own choice, not a rider instruction. EV-CHAT-00102 contains a single message, sent by the DRIVER at 11:29:04 — 'boss BKE quite jam, i go Upper Bukit Timah ok?' — and the rider never replied; message.waypoint_hint is null. POL-RD-04 requires the instruction to come from the rider and any corroborating waypoint to be read from chat_message.waypoint_hint rather than geocoded from general knowledge. With no rider message there is no instruction, and with a null hint the corroboration test cannot be run at all. The detour cannot be laid at the rider's door.

The driver's asserted external event is unevidenced, and the one artifact that could settle it — a traffic advisory for the BKE corridor — is missing and flagged BLOCKING. POL-RD-10 is addressed to precisely this situation: a traffic excuse asserted with no traffic_advisory is a matter the tribunal cannot resolve on the papers, and the disposition the policy prescribes is escalation rather than a final money ruling. Under POL-GEN-03 an ESCALATE is terminal and holds the disputed SGD 7.00 rather than collecting or refunding it, so it is the only disposition available on this record that leaves the rider not carrying the disputed charge while the driver's justification is tested.

claims.text: The governing distance figure is the trace, not the trip record. Under POL-RD-01 the excess is measured on gps_trace.trace_distance_km, which is 21.79 km against a booked optimal of 20.4 km, giving an excess of 1.39 km; trip_record.actual_distance_km (21.8 km) is a rounded convenience copy and may not be cited for the threshold test.

That excess is 6.81% of optimal, far below the 20% gate. POL-RD-01 requires the excess to be BOTH greater than 20% of optimal_distance_km AND greater than 0.8 km; the percentage limb fails even though the 1.39 km absolute limb passes, and because both tests must pass no route deviation is established on this trip.

The trace is unbroken and unimpaired: 193 fixes at a 10-second interval, 100% coverage, no gaps and a maximum gap of 0 seconds, and the platform's own deviation block records the status as 'no deviation'. POL-RD-07 is therefore not engaged, there is no impaired stretch to re-measure and the rider has no basis to recompute the excess in its own favour.

The rider's complaint is framed on elapsed time (32 minutes against a 27-minute estimate) and on preference ('not the route I would have taken'). POL-RD-01 is a distance test with a distance gate, and the distance gate is not met; a route the rider simply would not have chosen is not a refundable deviation.

The rider carries the initial burden under POL-RD-08 and must show an excess meeting the POL-RD-01 threshold measured from an unimpaired trace. The measured excess does not meet that threshold, so the initial burden is not discharged and it never shifts to the driver to invoke any exculpatory clause.

The materiality limb is not remotely approached: the excess of 1.39 km and 6.81% falls far below the 8.0 km and 50% material thresholds, so POL-RD-06's driver_profile check is not engaged. In any event the driver's 90-day record is clean, with deviation_flags_90d of 0 across 640 completed_trips_90d.

No separate pass-through or billing-integrity correction is due. The fare_breakdown carries no ERP gantries at all and no airport surcharge, and the trip did not originate at an airport, so POL-RD-09(4) has nothing to refund.

No driver compensation arises under POL-RD-04: the distance actually billed (21.8 km) is not less than the distance the trace records (21.79 km), so there is no unbilled shortfall exceeding 1.0 km to compensate at the per-kilometre rate.

The driver did not conceal the route choice: the chat log shows a single message, sent at 11:29, telling the rider 'boss BKE quite jam, i go Upper Bukit Timah ok?', delivered and read at 11:29:40. That is a communicated, modest re-route, and no instruction on any route ever came from the rider.

The correct outcome is NO_ACTION. Under POL-GEN-03 NO_ACTION is party-relative: this dispute was filed by the rider and the fare_breakdown shows payment_status CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd 0.0, so no-action leaves the present payment state exactly as it stands and returns nothing to the rider.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider and to the driver: this is trip TRP-00102 (Woodlands to ION Orchard) on 19 July 2026, and the question is whether any part of the SGD 29.91 fare, or the SGD 7.00 the rider disputes, should be returned.

The distance test fails, and that decides the case. Under POL-RD-01 the governing measurement is the GPS trace, not the trip record: the trace records 21.79 km against a booked optimal of 20.4 km, an excess of 1.39 km, or 6.81%. A route deviation is established only when the excess is BOTH more than 20% of the optimal AND more than 0.8 km. The 0.8 km limb passes; the 20% limb does not. Both must pass, so no deviation exists and the POL-RD-02 fare recomputation does not run. I have not used the trip record's actual_distance_km (21.8 km) for the threshold, because POL-RD-01 makes it a rounded convenience copy of the trace figure. The rider is right that the trip took 32 minutes against a 27-minute estimate, and right that this is not the route they would have taken; but POL-RD-01 is a distance test with a distance gate, and a route a rider simply would not have chosen is not a refundable deviation.

The trace is not impaired. It carries 193 fixes at a 10-second interval, with 100% coverage, no gaps and a maximum gap of 0 seconds, so POL-RD-07 is not engaged and there is no impaired stretch to re-measure.

On the driver's account of a BKE crawl: the only traffic advisory for this trip, EV-ADVIS-00102-01, is MISSING, with weight_multiplier 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT (BLOCKING). It carries no fact, and its absence is noted. The driver's traffic explanation is a general assertion of bad traffic; under POL-RD-08 an assertion unsupported by a traffic_advisory ID does not discharge the driver's burden. That does not, however, escalate this case: no exculpatory clause (POL-RD-03) was invoked — the driver's position is that there was no deviation to excuse — and the driver's burden never arose, because the rider's threshold showing failed first. The practical effect is only that the driver gets no exoneration, not that the rider gets a refund the distance test does not support.

On the rider's side: the trip identifiers and timestamps match across the trip record, the trace and the fare ledger, so POL-RD-08(a) is satisfied; but limb (b), an excess over threshold, is not, so the burden never shifts. The rider's own case is candid that no distance deviation is established.

No billing-integrity correction under POL-RD-09(4) is due: the fare breakdown carries no ERP gantries and no airport surcharge, and its lines reconcile to the 29.91 charged. No driver compensation under POL-RD-04 is due: the billed distance (21.8 km) is not less than the trace distance (21.79 km), so there is no unbilled shortfall. POL-RD-06 is not engaged: the excess is nowhere near material (8.0 km or 50%), and in any event the driver's 90-day record shows 0 deviation flags across 640 completed trips, so no conduct referral arises.

Outcome: NO_ACTION. Nothing is refunded and nothing is held; the fare stands as charged.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider: I understand the trip felt long and off the route you know, and that 32 minutes is five more than the 27-minute estimate. But POL-RD-01 measures a route deviation in distance, and both of its limbs must pass. The governing figure is the GPS trace, not the trip record's rounded convenience copy: the trace records 21.79 km against a booked optimal of 20.4 km, an excess of 1.39 km, or 6.81%. That clears the absolute limb (1.39 km > 0.8 km) but fails the relative limb (6.81% is far below 20%). Because both must pass, no deviation is established, and POL-RD-01 directs NO_ACTION however the trip is characterised. POL-RD-02 (the fare recomputation) therefore never runs, and the difference you paid is not refundable on this route. I have recorded that the three artifacts describe the same trip (POL-RD-08(a) is satisfied), but that does not help you, because the threshold showing under POL-RD-08(b) fails and the burden never shifts to the driver.

To the driver: I note your explanation that the BKE was crawling near Dairy Farm and that you came off via Upper Thomson, and the single in-app message to the rider at 11:29. But your traffic explanation cites no evidence ID, and POL-RD-08 provides that a general assertion that traffic was bad, unsupported by a traffic advisory, does not discharge anything. The only advisory artifact, EV-ADVIS-00102-01, is MISSING: it carries weight_multiplier 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT (BLOCKING), and the record confirms no LTA advisory covers the BKE or the Upper Bukit Timah corridor in the trip window. Under POL-GEN-02(3) I name that artifact and its weight, and I confirm it cannot carry any fact. This does not change the outcome, because with no deviation established there is nothing for POL-RD-03 or POL-RD-04 to excuse; but you should not treat the missing advisory as support for the re-route.

Common ground: the trace is unbroken (193 fixes, 10-second sampling, 100% coverage, no gaps, max gap 0 s), so POL-RD-07 is not engaged and no stretch needs re-measuring. The chat log contains one driver message with no rider reply and a null waypoint_hint, so POL-RD-04 is unavailable: no rider instruction exists and the corroboration test cannot be run at all. The fare breakdown carries no ERP gantries and no airport surcharge and reconciles to the cent, so POL-RD-09 has nothing to correct; and the distance billed (21.8 km) is not less than the traced distance (21.79 km), so no driver compensation arises under POL-RD-04. The driver's profile shows deviation_flags_90d of 0 over 640 completed trips in 90 days, so POL-RD-06 is not engaged and no conduct referral is made.

Outcome: NO_ACTION. Under POL-GEN-03 no-action is party-relative: this dispute was filed by the rider and the fare stands CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd 0.0, so the present payment state is left exactly as it is. No money moves and no referral is issued. No mandatory escalation applies: the trace is unimpaired under POL-RD-07, the trip identifiers all match, no timestamps conflict, no charge line is unmatched, and no exculpatory clause was invoked against a cited artifact, so POL-RD-10 is not engaged. Confidence is 0.95, resting on the trace and trip record, both at full weight. One open point for the platform (not a ground for escalation here, since the distance test decides the case): the LTA advisory feed has no coverage for that corridor and window, and that data gap is worth closing.

To the rider: I understand the frustration — the driver did leave the BKE and the trip ran 32 minutes against a 27-minute estimate. But a route-deviation claim is decided on distance, and on the distance this trip was not a deviation. The governing measurement is the GPS trace, which records 21.79 km (the trip record's 21.8 km is a rounded convenience copy of the same measurement and is not used for the threshold test). Against the booked optimal of 20.4 km that is an excess of 1.39 km, or 6.81%. POL-RD-01 requires the excess to exceed BOTH 0.8 km and 20% of optimal; 1.39 km clears the absolute limb but 6.81% does not clear the relative limb, and because both must pass, no deviation is established. No deviation means no route-deviation refund and no fare recomputation under POL-RD-02, so the $7.00 you contest is not refundable on this ground.

To the driver: the outcome is in your favour, but not because of the traffic excuse. Because the rider's threshold was not met, the burden never shifted to you under POL-RD-08, so there was nothing to exculpate and no exculpatory clause needed to run. I have not relied on your account of a BKE crawl. The traffic-advisory artifact EV-ADVIS-00102-01 is MISSING, weight_multiplier 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT (BLOCKING); it carries no fact and I have not used it. I mention it only because the rider raised it. Its absence does not change the outcome and does not force an escalation, because no exculpatory clause was invoked against it and no deviation needed excusing.

On the remaining points. The trace is unimpaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07: 193 fixes at a 10-second interval, 100% coverage, no gaps, maximum gap 0 seconds; there is therefore no impaired stretch to re-measure and no corroboration question. No material deviation exists, so the POL-RD-06 driver-profile check is not engaged. The fare breakdown carries no ERP gantries and no airport surcharge, and the trip did not originate at an airport, so POL-RD-09(4) has nothing to correct; the line items reconcile exactly to the $29.91 charged (base 3.80 + distance 16.35 + time 8.96 + platform fee 0.80). The distance billed, 21.8 km, is not less than the distance the trace records, so there is no unbilled shortfall exceeding 1.0 km and no driver compensation under POL-RD-04. The rider's same-trip showing under POL-RD-08(a) is accepted, and the rider is right that no rider instruction appears in the chat log, but both points are moot once the threshold fails.

Outcome: NO_ACTION. Under POL-GEN-03 this is party-relative; the claim is not supported by the evidence and the present payment state stands — payment_status remains CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd 0.0. No clause produces a referral on these facts.

ledger.claim: The artifacts describe the same trip and satisfy the rider's initial showing under POL-RD-08(a): EV-TRIP-00102, EV-GPS-00102 and EV-FARE-00102 all carry trip_id TRP-00102; the trip record's started_at (2026-07-19T11:23:30+08:00) is identical to the trace's first_fix_at, and the ledger's charged_at (11:55:48) sits immediately after the trace's last_fix_at (11:55:30). Same vehicle, same rider, same trip.

Under POL-RD-01 the governing distance figure is the trace, not the rounded convenience copy: gps_trace.trace_distance_km is 21.79 km against trip_record.actual_distance_km of 21.8 km, and the platform's own derived block measures the excess over the 20.4 km optimal at 1.39 km, or 6.81%. On the governing figure the excess clears the absolute limb (1.39 km > 0.8 km) but not the relative limb (6.81% < 20%), and POL-RD-01 requires both to pass. The rider is candid that a distance deviation is therefore not established and does not press a POL-RD-02 recomputation. What the rider does contest is the driver's justification for leaving the booked corridor at all.

The driver's account rests on a BKE crawl, and there is nothing behind it. The only advisory artifact, EV-ADVIS-00102-01, is MISSING — weight_multiplier 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT (BLOCKING) — and its own issue detail states that no LTA advisory covers the BKE or the Upper Bukit Timah corridor in the 11:16-11:55 window on 19 July 2026. That absence is itself citable. Without an advisory the driver cannot satisfy the three limbs of POL-RD-03: there is no advisory naming an affected road or segment, no validity window, and no shortest_lawful_alternative_km from which the capped justified excess could be computed. POL-RD-08 then provides that a general assertion that traffic was bad, unsupported by a traffic_advisory ID, does not discharge the driver's burden.

The diversion was the driver's own choice, not a rider instruction. EV-CHAT-00102 contains a single message, sent by the DRIVER at 11:29:04 — 'boss BKE quite jam, i go Upper Bukit Timah ok?' — and the rider never replied; message.waypoint_hint is null. POL-RD-04 requires the instruction to come from the rider and any corroborating waypoint to be read from chat_message.waypoint_hint rather than geocoded from general knowledge. With no rider message there is no instruction, and with a null hint the corroboration test cannot be run at all. The detour cannot be laid at the rider's door.

The driver's asserted external event is unevidenced, and the one artifact that could settle it — a traffic advisory for the BKE corridor — is missing and flagged BLOCKING. POL-RD-10 is addressed to precisely this situation: a traffic excuse asserted with no traffic_advisory is a matter the tribunal cannot resolve on the papers, and the disposition the policy prescribes is escalation rather than a final money ruling. Under POL-GEN-03 an ESCALATE is terminal and holds the disputed SGD 7.00 rather than collecting or refunding it, so it is the only disposition available on this record that leaves the rider not carrying the disputed charge while the driver's justification is tested.

POL-RD-01 is a distance test with a distance gate, and the distance gate is not met; a route the rider simply would not have chosen is not a refundable deviation.

The rider carries the initial burden under POL-RD-08 and must show an excess meeting the POL-RD-01 threshold measured from an unimpaired trace. The measured excess does not meet that threshold, so the initial burden is not discharged and it never shifts to the driver to invoke any exculpatory clause.

The materiality limb is not remotely approached: the excess of 1.39 km and 6.81% falls far below the 8.0 km and 50% material thresholds, so POL-RD-06's driver_profile check is not engaged.
